text:
alice: Quick share — ran a lightweight flowbench comparing streaming vs non-streaming endpoints for a new bring-up (redwood-alpaca-13b-qint8). Regions: us-west (A100), eu-west (H100), ap-sg (T4). TL;DR: streaming mode increases steady-state throughput but shows worse tail in bursty fanout. charts: https://perf.internal/flowbench/2178001234 :thumbsup:

ben: Nice. what's the client pattern + payload?

carmen: Replayed a real customer QPS trace (30m). Prompt 32 tokens, gen target 512, median request size ~280 tokens. Concurrency target: median 120 req/s per region, bursts to 1k req/s for 15s.

devon: Kernel stack and quantization? KV cache on?

carmen: Quant: int8/q4_0. Runtime: fused-attn + nvFlash on H100/A100, cuBLAS fallback on T4. KV cache enabled and pinned per-connection for streaming; non-streaming endpoints share ephemeral KV.

alice: Raw numbers (approx):
- us-west A100: streaming: 9.2k tokens/s, p50 38ms, p95 190ms; non-streaming: 5.1k tokens/s, p50 44ms, p95 120ms.
- eu-west H100: streaming: 12.6k tokens/s, p50 30ms, p95 160ms; non-streaming: 7.0k tokens/s, p50 36ms, p95 100ms.
- ap-sg T4: streaming: 3.0k tokens/s, p50 110ms, p95 420ms; non-streaming: 1.8k tokens/s, p50 130ms, p95 260ms.

ben: So streaming wins on throughput (makes sense: continuous emit + KV reuse) but p95 sometimes worse because of head-of-line/backpressure during bursts?

carmen: Exactly. Streaming keeps tx path hot so steady throughput up, but when client fanout spikes we saw queueing in the stream writer -> long tails. Non-streaming batches requests more aggressively which smooths tails but reduces overall tokens/s.

devon: Any kernel sensitivity? e.g., softpin / allocator changes?

carmen: Yes. On A100/H100 the nvFlash kernel improves perf for seq<=512 by ~18%. Turning on softpin (cpu->gpu affinity) reduced p95 by ~20% on streaming under burst. On T4 we hit cuBLAS limits; batching strategy matters more.

ben: Did you test smaller micro-batches to trade latency vs throughput?

carmen: Ran a sweep: micro-batch sizes {1,2,4,8}. For streaming: batch=2 gave best p50+p95 balance. For non-streaming endpoints batch=8 increased throughput but p50 rose by ~10-15ms.

alice: Repro command snippet used for the run: 
```
./flowbench --model redwood-alpaca-13b-qint8 --mode streaming --region us-west --gpu a100 --trace replay.json --concurrency 120 --duration 1800 --kv-cache on --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8
```

deploy-bot: perf-run uploaded: https://perf.internal/artifacts/2178001234 (charts + raw logs).

carmen: Notes on quality/regression: quant int8 kept ROUGE/MT metrics within 1.5% of fp16 for this prompt set. Need larger eval set before shipping. Also saw occasional token corruption on T4 under extreme bursts (possible memory pressure).

devon: Ops actionables?

alice: Proposed next steps:
- carmen: run 99/99.9 tail runs with cold caches + longer burst profile (30m) in us-west and eu-west.
- ben: test softpin+oom-guard on A100 and see if streaming tail improves further.
- devon: use these numbers to update Dedicated capacity calculator (assume steady streaming throughput for pricing, but add headroom for p95 tail).

carmen: I'll kick off the 99.9 tail runs this afternoon and post a follow-up thread with updated charts.

ben: If we want a quick stopgap for customers: add per-connection write-rate limiter on streaming to reduce HOL tail at the cost of slightly lower peak throughput.

alice: Agreed. Thanks all — will sync with product on whether to recommend streaming for enterprise Dedicated or keep non-streaming as default for sensitive SLAs.
